creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Now concrete rather than speculative, because the measurements exist (observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 12).

What is already true: herdr restores its own session shape across a daemon restart - pane ids, tree, cwds - and loses every process and all scrollback. layout.export/layout.apply round-trip a tree with cwds, though apply is additive rather than reconciling.

What a real 'resume' would add on top: per pane, the harness's own session reference, so a restored pane relaunches its agent with --resume rather than fresh. herdr already carries the pointer (pane.report_agent_session, taking agent_session_id or agent_session_path); nothing reports it today.

The open questions, in the order they matter:
- Do we commit to a restore feature at all, or is the daemon's own recovery enough? Naming matters here: 'restore layout' promises what it can deliver, 'resume' promises conversation state we cannot.
- Who reports the agent session reference? Muster is well placed to, but inferring one by reading agent output is the agent-framework non-goal. Only a reference the harness hands over is metadata.
- Cross-daemon restore is ours by elimination - herdr's export cannot describe a workspace spanning a laptop and a devenv. Is that worth building before multi-daemon exists at all?

Most of the leverage is upstream. Material for a_26BJbJeZL.
title: Restore a workspace: how far do we go, and whose job is it?
